newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ifo says Bonn to qualify for EMU despite overshoot.
newsitem.headline: Ifo says Bonn to qualify for EMU despite overshoot.

text.p: The Ifo economic institute forecast on Thursday Germany's 1997 budget deficit to exceed the Maastricht ceiling, but said that would not preclude it from qualifying for monetary union.

Ifo President Karl-Heinrich Oppenlaender said in a speech prepared for the institute's annual meeting that Germany's overall 1997 state budget deficit would be just under 120 billion marks, or 3.2 percent of gross domestic product (GDP). The forecast did not take into account new saving measures discussed by Bonn.
The Maastricht Treaty sets a ceiling of three percent for joining the Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) but allows leeway in certain circumstances.

"I nevertheless believe that with such a deficit, Germany will not be denied entry to European monetary union since the Maastricht Treaty allows certain divergence from the reference target," Oppenlaender said.
"The public has the impression that even small decimal point divergence from the three percent level would endanger the stability of the future currency. This is wrong," he said.
"We should therefore end the decimal point discussion about this year's deficit as quickly as possible."
He said that the stability of the euro was far more dependent on the monetary policy conducted by the European Central Bank in 1999.
He said a sustainable and solid fiscal policy was necessary to make the job of the European Central Bank easier.
